name: Verde River (White Bridge to Beasley Flat)
gaugeName: Verde River near Camp Verde, AZ
blurb: The classic Camp Verde canoe and kayak float from White Bridge to Beasley Flat, Prescott National Forest. Clear Creek is a rough mid-point access.

sections.putIn: White Bridge Picnic Site and Boat Launch (Verde)
sections.notes: Prescott NF: Beasley Flat is the 'most popular take-out spot for canoes and kayaks after a 10-mile float from White Bridge.' AZ State Parks Paddle Map 3: White Bridge (RM 39.5) to Clear Creek 5.5 mi, Clear Creek to Beasley (RM 49.3) 4.3 mi. Hazards on the map: minor irrigation dam, rock bars, tree fence, tree tunnel, Class 2 riffles. Take out at Beasley: below it the Wild & Scenic run is for experienced boaters only (Verde Falls Class IV at mile 2.5).

guideTimes.conditions: Derived by adding the guide’s two adjoining legs via Clear Creek: 4 hours at its medium-flow category, 6 hours at low flow. These are guide totals, not an observed trip. Numeric flow bands, craft and stops are not specified.
guideTimes.sourceName: Arizona State Parks-hosted Verde River Paddle Map 3, page 3 (2013 guide)

putInAccess.sourceName: USDA Forest Service, Prescott NF: White Bridge Picnic Site and Boat Launch + Verde River page
putInAccess.note: Agency point is 168 m from the NHD centreline (>150 m). Official source names boating access, but the exact water-entry point is not pinned by an agency coordinate confirmed on imagery. Restrictions:
putInAccess.directions: Just off Highway 260 (Prescott NF page); a short walk leads to the river.

takeOutAccess.operator: USDA Forest Service (Prescott NF, Verde RD)
takeOutAccess.sourceName: Access: USDA Forest Service, Prescott NF: Beasley Flat Picnic Site; AZ State Parks Paddle Map 2 (Mile 0.0). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking (owner-supplied), checked on Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate is owner-supplied (North's own Google Maps satellite marking, 34.4734529, -111.8012007) and checked on Esri World Imagery z19 on 2026-10-26 (research/raw/imagery/beasley_flat_verde_owner_z19.png); it is NOT an agency coordinate. On imagery: North's point sits in a bare sandy clearing that runs through a gap in the west-bank riparian trees to open water, about 8 m from the waterline, directly east of the paved Beasley Flat picnic loop. The concrete ramp surface the paddle guide describes is not clearly distinguishable on the imagery, but this is the only open shore gap by the loop road. The USFS EDW point (recareaid 67209) plots in the channel about 340 m north-northeast. NHD High Resolution flowline 28 m away. Superseded agency point: USFS EDW Recreation Opportunities, recareaid 67209 'Beasley Flat Picnic Site' (Prescott NF page: 34.47651531, -111.8007081) at 34.476515, -111.800708 (https://apps.fs.usda.gov/arcx/rest/services/EDW/EDW_RecreationOpportunities_01/MapServer/0/query?where=recareaid%3D67209&outFields=*&outSR=4326&f=json). Legal boating access: USDA Forest Service, Prescott NF: Beasley Flat Picnic Site; AZ State Parks Paddle Map 2 (Mile 0.0) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/prescott/recreation/beasley-flat-picnic-site): 'It is also the most popular take-out spot for canoes and kayaks after a 10-mile float from White Bridge.' Paddle Map 2: Beasley Flat facilities 'include a concrete boat ramp, a parking lot, toilets'. Spot-check this point first; imagery date is not published by Esri.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHD High Resolution flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~179), the point is right of the NHD centreline (28 m). The access road, picnic loop and launch clearing are on the west bank (river right when facing downstream, flow to the south).
